nodes.title: fs.rmSync fails on read-only file with EPERM
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

`fs.rmSync` should delete the file even if it's read-only.

### Actual Behavior

`fs.rmSync` in Electron preload (nodeIntegration: true) fails to delete read-only file with: EPERM, Permission denied (Note: Windows 11). See the Gits Fiddle. Press "Create RO file" and then "Remove RO file".

While `fsPromises.rm` removes the file OK.

Node.version in Electron 43.0.0 is 24.17.0. When I try it with standalone Node.js 24.17.0 from command line, then the file is deleted OK.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/5042e7e0b320461ca0bb86908239bd5b

### Additional Information

Note:
- I have not tried it in electron main process without nodeIntegration. This is not used in public code, just internal one and we want to keep it KISS.
- It was working with some older Electron version.

nodes.title: Replacing menu while open causes segfault on Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10.0.19045 (6466)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Calling `Menu.setApplicationMenu()` while the user interacts with an open menu should not crash the app.

### Actual Behavior

If the application menu is replaced while being displayed, and a GC triggers before the menu closes, the relevant `Menu` object will be garbage-collected, causing various kinds of segfaults in menu-related UI code.

For example:
```
OS Version: Windows 10.0.19045 (6466)
Report Version: 104

Crashed Thread: 38224

Application Specific Information:
Fatal Error: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ / 0x0

Thread 38224 Crashed:
0   Figma.exe                       0x7ff6274073c7      ui::MenuModel::GetModelAndIndexForCommandId (menu_model.cc:49)
1   Figma.exe                       0x7ff62a4fd728      views::MenuModelAdapter::GetLabelFontList (menu_model_adapter.cc:225)
2   Figma.exe                       0x7ff62a507cdf      views::MenuItemView::GetFontList (menu_item_view.cc:1005)
3   Figma.exe                       0x7ff62a505f35      views::MenuItemView::OnPaintImpl (menu_item_view.cc:1115)
4   Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987cfb      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1475)
5   Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
6   Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
7   Figma.exe                       0x7ff62a502328      views::SubmenuView::PaintChildren (submenu_view.cc:316)
8   Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
9   Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
10  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
11  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
12  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
13  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
14  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
15  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
16  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
17  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
18  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620988261      views::View::RecursivePaintHelper (view.cc:3114)
19  Figma.exe                       0x7ff62098811f      views::View::PaintChildren (view.cc:2436)
20  Figma.exe                       0x7ff620987d6f      views::View::Paint (view.cc:1481)
21  Figma.exe                       0x7ff622ce48fe      views::View::PaintFromPaintRoot (view.cc:3122)
22  Figma.exe                       0x7ff622d60191      ui::Layer::PaintContentsToDisplayList (layer.cc:1599)
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/rf-figma/103e9c2d491975cbefe183bfa5ca3cc5

### Additional Information

To trigger the issue in Fiddle, you need to run the app with `--js-flags=--expose-gc`, open the File menu, and mouse over the menu a bit.

This issue was introduced in 41.2.1, almost definitely in #50915 (the backport of #50465).

That PR contains a bunch of GC-related changes, one of which was the removal of a `gin_helper::SelfKeepAlive` property from `Menu`. I think [the premise of the change was that this was redundant](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50806#pullrequestreview-4079112260), since `Menu` instances are all owned by other objects that should retain them properly.

The problem with this is that the owner of a `Menu` will only retain it as long as it hasn't been replaced. If you replace the menu while it's open, and the `Menu` object gets garbage-collected as a result, its destructor will clear all of the delegate pointers that are still being used by the rendered views.

I tried just restoring the `SelfKeepAlive` and it did fix the issue for me, although I'm not sure if there's some reason that we would need to do this differently now. I'll put up a PR in a second.

nodes.title: desktopCapturer returns sources with empty `display_id` on Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Sources returned by desktopCapturer should have a valid `display_id` property when using a capturer other than DirectX on Windows. There is a bug in code https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/57cc00ce06d2a1dc222bb2c358dcd82cfd57ab13/shell/browser/api/electron_api_desktop_capturer.cc#L485 for Windows path `display_id` is only initlialized when `using_directx_capturer_ = true `. Moreover `using_directx_capturer_` should be set based on actual usage, now it only checks if DirectX capturer is supported, while GDI Capturer can be used as a fallback. This will also cause errors in the future for the WGC capturer. 

### Actual Behavior

`display_id = ''`

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/michalzaq12/52be3585397f508a3c4c67f5c14f8004

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: [Bug]: globalShortcut portal path collapses F-key and punctuation accelerators to the same command id
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (any version with the Wayland GlobalShortcuts portal path)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Any Linux Wayland session using the org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts path

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Expected Behavior

Registering two shortcuts like `Ctrl+F9` and `Ctrl+F10` on the Wayland portal path binds two distinct portal shortcuts.

### Actual Behavior

`GlobalShortcut::Register` builds the portal command id from `extensions::Command::AcceleratorToString(accelerator)`, which only supports A–Z, 0–9, comma, period, arrows, Home/End/PgUp/PgDn, Space, Tab, Insert/Delete, and the media keys — everything else (all F-keys, Escape, Enter, most punctuation, numpad) returns an empty string. All such accelerators therefore collapse to the same empty command id and the same fake extension id, colliding in `command_callback_map_` and in the portal session: only the last registered shortcut of that class is actually bound, and its activation runs the last-registered callback.

Observed empirically: registering `Control+Shift+F9` produces a portal command whose id is derived from an empty accelerator string.

### Additional Information

Two possible directions: extend the stringification used for portal command ids to cover all registrable accelerators (needs to stay stable across versions, since the portal persists binds keyed by these ids), or key commands by something independent of the accelerator (with a migration for existing persisted binds). Related plumbing work: #52218.

nodes.title: A configurable build system using a file like electron.config.js
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

While working on several Electron projects, I noticed that many desktop applications don't actually use a large portion of the Chromium features that are included by default.

Applications such as launchers, utilities, configuration tools, local dashboards, media managers, or internal business software often only need the rendering engine and a few web APIs. Features like the built-in PDF viewer, Wallet, Translate, Media Router, and similar browser functionality may never be used, yet they are still bundled with every application.

It would be nice if developers had a way to avoid shipping optional Chromium features that their application doesn't need.

### Proposed Solution

One possible approach would be to introduce a build configuration file, something similar to `electron.config.js`, where developers could enable or disable supported Chromium components before packaging.

For example:

```js
module.exports = {
  chromium: {
    pdfViewer: false,
    wallet: false,
    translate: false,
    mediaRouter: false,
    autofill: false
  }
};
```

If no configuration file is present, Electron would continue to behave exactly as it does today.

Only components that are considered optional and safe to exclude would be configurable. Anything required by Electron or Chromium would simply remain enabled.

### Alternatives Considered

I also thought about having separate Electron distributions, such as a "minimal" build and a "full" build.

However, I think a configuration-based approach would be more flexible. Different applications have different requirements, so allowing developers to choose which optional features they need seems more practical than maintaining multiple Electron distributions.

### Additional Information

I understand that Chromium has many internal dependencies and that not every feature can simply be removed.

The goal isn't to make every Chromium component optional, but to provide a supported way to exclude features that are already considered optional.

Even if only a small number of components could be configured this way, it could still help reduce application size and avoid shipping functionality that some applications will never use.

nodes.title: [Bug]: globalShortcut.register() returns true before the Wayland portal bind resolves
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (also 42.5.1 with the portal path enabled via flags)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (GNOME Wayland, gnome-shell 50.1, xdg-desktop-portal 1.21.1)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

On the Linux Wayland portal path, an app can find out whether a `globalShortcut.register()` call actually resulted in a bound shortcut — or at minimum, `register()`/`isRegistered()` should not report success when the portal denied the bind.

### Actual Behavior

On Wayland, `globalShortcut` goes through the `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts` portal (`GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux`). The portal's `BindShortcuts` call is asynchronous and consent-gated (GNOME shows a dialog before binding), so the synchronous boolean returned by `register()` cannot be truthful on this path: `GlobalShortcut::Register()` returns `true` as soon as the command set is handed to the listener via `OnCommandsChanged()`, before the bind resolves. `isRegistered()` is equally misleading — it only consults the local command map.

If the portal later replies with an error — e.g. GNOME 50.0/50.1 rejects `BindShortcuts` for any app id that fails `g_application_id_is_valid()` (see gnome-control-center `global-shortcuts-provider`; relaxed in 50.2), or the user dismisses the consent dialog — the result dies in `GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux::OnBindShortcuts()` as a `LOG(ERROR)`. Nothing reaches `ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener` observers, so Electron has no way to surface it even if it wanted to.

Observed on an Ubuntu 26.04 VM with stock Electron binaries (`GlobalShortcutsPortal` + `GlobalShortcutsPortalPreferredTrigger` enabled):

```
# invalid app id (dashed desktopName, no dot): register() lies, portal denies
20:32:28 REGISTER Control+Shift+F9 -> true
dbus: error_name=org.freedesktop.portal.Error.NotAllowed reply_serial=23
(shortcut never fires, no dialog shown)

# valid reverse-DNS desktopName (com.example.MyApp.desktop): works end to end
20:41:49 REGISTER Control+Shift+F9 -> true
20:44:34 FIRED Control+Shift+F10        # after one consent dialog
20:46:38 REGISTER ... -> true            # relaunch: silent re-bind, persists
```

Apps cannot distinguish three genuinely different states: **bound**, **pending consent**, and **denied**. That matters in practice — "shortcut silently doesn't work" is indistinguishable from "user hasn't clicked the consent dialog yet".

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Surfacing the bind result needs a small Chromium patch: `OnBindShortcuts()` receives the response but `ui::GlobalAcceleratorListener` has no observer/callback for it today.

Proposed minimal API (shape open for discussion): keep `register()` synchronous — its boolean means "request submitted" on this path — and add a module event that fires when the portal resolves the bind:

```js
globalShortcut.on('registration-resolved', (accelerator, bound) => {
  // bound === false: portal denied (invalid app id, user dismissed dialog, ...)
})
```

Alternatives considered: a promise-returning `registerAsync()`, or a callback in an options object. On non-portal platforms the event could fire immediately with the `register()` result, keeping it usable cross-platform.

Draft PR with plumbing to follow; API shape needs API WG input.
